title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION ACT
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION ACT

Article 1 (Purpose)

The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the National Human Rights Commission Act and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Protective Facilities for Multiple Persons)

The term "facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 2, subparagraph 2 (e) of the National Human Rights Commission Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means the following facilities: <Amended on May 29, 2017; August 18, 2026>
1. Child welfare facilities: Child care facilities, temporary child protection facilities, child protection and treatment facilities, group homes, and self-reliance support facilities under Article 52 (1) 1 through 5 of the Child Welfare Act;
2. Welfare facilities for persons with disabilities: Residential facilities for persons with disabilities under Article 58 (1) 1 of the Welfare of Persons with Disabilities Act;
3. Mental health promotion facilities: Psychiatric medical institutions (limited to those equipped with accommodation facilities), mental health nursing facilities, and mental rehabilitation facilities under Article 3, subparagraphs 5 through 7 of the Act on the Improvement of Mental Health and the Support for Welfare Services for Mental Patients;
4. Welfare facilities for homeless persons: Temporary protection facilities for homeless persons, self-reliance facilities for homeless persons, rehabilitation facilities for homeless persons, and nursing facilities for homeless persons under Article 16 (1) 1 through 4 of the Act on Support for the Welfare and Self-Reliance of Homeless Persons, etc.;
5. Welfare facilities for older persons:
(a) Residential welfare facilities for older persons: Homes for older persons and group homes for older persons under Article 32 (1) 1 and 2 of the Welfare of Senior Citizens Act;
(b) Medical welfare facilities for older persons: Nursing facilities for older persons and group nursing homes for older persons under Article 34 (1) 1 and 2 of the Welfare of Senior Citizens Act;
6. Support facilities for victims of prostitution, etc.: General support facilities, support facilities for juveniles, and support facilities for foreigners under Article 9 (1) 1 through 3 of the Act on the Prevention of Prostitution and Protection, etc. of Victims;
7. Rehabilitation facilities: Facilities established for rehabilitation services by a person licensed to conduct rehabilitation services under Article 67 of the Act on Probation, etc. (limited to those equipped with accommodation facilities);
8. Welfare facilities for single-parent families: Childbirth support facilities, child-rearing support facilities, livelihood support facilities, and temporary support facilities under Article 19 (1) 1 through 4 of the Single-Parent Family Support Act.

Article 3 (On-Site Visits to Detention and Protective Facilities)

(1) Where the National Human Rights Commission (hereinafter referred to as the "Commission") intends to conduct an on-site visit pursuant to Article 24 (1) of the Act, it shall notify the head or administrator of the relevant detention and protective facility in advance of the purpose, date and time, place, etc. of the visit: Provided, That this shall not apply in urgent cases or where prior notification is deemed likely to make it difficult to achieve the purpose of the investigation.
(2) A human rights commissioner under Article 5 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "commissioner"), a member of the Commission's staff, or an expert (hereinafter collectively referred to as "commissioners, etc.") who conducts an on-site visit pursuant to Article 24 (2) of the Act may request necessary assistance from the head of a relevant administrative agency where deemed necessary. <Amended on July 1, 2022>
(3) Commissioners, etc. who conduct on-site visits pursuant to Article 24 (2) of the Act may, where deemed necessary, conduct investigations using the following methods:
1. Hearing statements from staff of detention and protective facilities, persons housed in detention and protective facilities (hereinafter referred to as "facility residents"), etc.;
2. Requiring the head or administrator of a detention and protective facility to submit necessary materials and receiving such materials;
3. Verifying objects, persons, places, and other circumstances as necessary through audio recording, video recording, photography, examination of the health status of facility residents, etc.
(4) Audio or video recordings made pursuant to paragraph (3) 3 shall be used solely for purposes of investigation, such as ascertaining the purport of the relevant statements or the condition of the subject of investigation, and shall not be publicly disclosed in their originally recorded form.
(5) Commissioners, etc. who conduct on-site visits pursuant to Article 24 (2) of the Act shall, upon completing an on-site visit to a detention and protective facility, enter the details thereof in an on-site visit record.
(6) Matters necessary for preparing on-site visit records under paragraph (5) shall be prescribed by rules of the Commission. <Amended on August 18, 2026>

Article 4 (Interviews with Facility Residents)
(1) Where commissioners, etc. interview facility residents pursuant to Article 24(4) of the Act, the head or administrator of the detention and protective facility shall provide a place where the interviews can be conducted in an atmosphere that permits free expression.
(2) Commissioners, etc. who interview facility residents pursuant to Article 24(4) of the Act may request the head or administrator of the detention and protective facility to limit the number of staff members of the facility present at the place of interview, and the head or administrator shall comply unless there are special grounds not to do so. <Amended on January 5, 2021>
(3) Staff members of a detention and protective facility who are present at a place where commissioners, etc. interview facility residents pursuant to Article 24(4) of the Act shall not participate in the interview without the permission of the commissioners, etc., and shall not obstruct the statements of facility residents by such means as expressing their own opinions. <Amended on January 5, 2021>

Article 5 (Protective Measures Following Investigative Interviews)
(1) A commissioner interviewing facility residents pursuant to Article 24(4) of the Act may request the head or administrator of the detention and protective facility to take preventive measures if there is a risk that a staff member of the facility or a facility resident may suffer physical harm, harm to health, or other disadvantages on account of the interview.
(2) Where the head or administrator of a detention and protective facility takes measures under paragraph (1), the head or administrator shall immediately notify the Commission of their details.

Article 6 (Notification of Methods for Filing Petitions, etc.)
(1) When first taking a facility resident into protection or custody, the head or administrator of a detention and protective facility shall inform the resident that they may file a petition concerning human rights violations with the Commission and of the method for doing so.
(2) The head or administrator of a detention and protective facility shall keep a guide stating that petitions concerning human rights violations may be filed with the Commission and explaining how to do so in a place where facility residents can consult it at all times.

Article 7 (Installation and Operation of Petition Boxes)
(1) The head of a detention and protective facility shall install a petition box at an appropriate place within the facility and provide paper, writing implements, and sealable envelopes.
(2) Where the head or administrator of a detention and protective facility installs a petition box under paragraph (1), the head or administrator shall notify the Commission of the location of the petition box.
(3) The head or administrator of a detention and protective facility shall ensure that facility residents can personally place their petitions in envelopes, seal them, and put them in the petition box.
(4) Public officials or staff members of a detention and protective facility shall check at a designated time each day whether the petition box contains petitions or written documents prepared by facility residents for submission to the Commission, and shall forward any such petitions or written documents to the Commission without delay.
(5) The form of the sealable envelopes under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by the rules of the Commission. <Amended on August 18, 2026>

Article 8 (Prohibition on Reading Written Documents Sent by the Commission)
Where a public official or staff member of a detention and protective facility opens correspondence bearing the Commission's name and confirms that it is correspondence sent by the Commission to a facility resident who is a petitioner, the official or staff member shall not read any specific written document in that correspondence that the Commission has requested not be read.

Article 9 (Freedom to Prepare and Submit Petitions)
(1) Where a facility resident expresses to the head or administrator of a detention and protective facility an intention to prepare a petition or other written document addressed to the Commission, the head or administrator shall neither prohibit nor obstruct its preparation.
(2) Public officials or staff members of a detention and protective facility shall not read, seize, or destroy a petition or written document that a facility resident is preparing or possesses for the purpose of sending it to the Commission. However, this shall not apply to a document being prepared or possessed without prior expression of the intention to prepare it under paragraph (1).
(3) Public officials or staff members of a detention and protective facility shall not take measures restricting a facility resident's opportunity to prepare or submit a petition or written document for transmission to the Commission on the grounds that the resident is being investigated for an alleged disciplinary offense or is undergoing disciplinary punishment.

Article 10 (Receipt of Petitions During Visits)
Paragraphs (3) and (4) of Article 3 shall apply mutatis mutandis where commissioners, etc. visit detention and protective facilities to receive petitions pursuant to Article 31(4) of the Act.

Article 11 (Notice of Visits)
Paragraphs (1) through (4) of Article 3 shall apply mutatis mutandis where commissioners, etc. visit a particular place or facility pursuant to Article 36(2) of the Act.

Article 12 (Applications for Challenge)
(1) A party wishing to challenge a commissioner or a member of a mediation committee under Article 41 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a “mediation committee member”) pursuant to Article 38(2) of the Act shall submit an application to the chairperson specifying the grounds for the challenge.
(2) A party who has filed an application for challenge shall submit the grounds for the challenge and the means of substantiating those grounds in writing within 3 days from the date of application.
(3) A commissioner or mediation committee member who is the subject of an application for challenge shall submit a written opinion on the application to the chairperson without delay.

Article 13 (Disposition of Applications for Challenge)
The chairperson shall dismiss an application for challenge that violates Article 12(1) or (2).

Article 14 (Suspension of Proceedings for Adopting Resolutions)
Where an application for exclusion or challenge is filed under Article 38(1) or (2) of the Act, proceedings for adopting resolutions shall be suspended until a decision on the application is made: Provided, That this shall not apply in cases requiring urgent action.

Article 15 (Voluntary Recusal of Commissioners)
(1) A commissioner or mediation committee member seeking voluntary recusal under Article 38(3) of the Act shall obtain the permission of the chairperson. <Amended on July 1, 2022>
(2) Where an application for voluntary recusal is deemed well-founded, the chairperson shall grant permission without delay.

Article 16 (Designation of Commissioners to Subcommittees)
Where a commissioner serving on a subcommittee under Article 12 of the Act becomes unable to perform the relevant duties due to exclusion, challenge, or voluntary recusal, the chairperson shall designate another commissioner to perform those duties without delay.

Article 17 (Expert Advisers)
Where deemed necessary to efficiently support the Commission’s work and conduct specialized investigations and research, expert advisers may be appointed within budgetary limits.

Article 18 (Payment of Travel Expenses, Etc.)
The Commission may, within budgetary limits, pay travel expenses and allowances to relevant persons who appear before the Commission in connection with its activities.

Article 19 (Establishment and Composition of the Human Rights Policy Officials Council)
(1) A Human Rights Policy Officials Council (hereinafter referred to as the “Council”) shall be established within the Commission to facilitate efficient consultations with relevant agencies and other entities under Article 20(2) of the Act.
(2) The secretary-general of the Commission shall serve as the chair of the Council (hereinafter referred to as the “Council chair”), and the following persons shall serve as its members:
1. Public officials in the Senior Civil Service serving in central administrative agencies who are designated by the heads of those central administrative agencies;
2. Public officials at the director-general level or above of a Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, or Special Self-Governing Do, designated by the relevant Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayor, Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Do Governor, or Special Self-Governing Do Governor;
3. Public officials at the director-general level or above of the office of education of a Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, or Special Self-Governing Do, designated by the superintendent of education;
4. Other persons deemed to possess extensive knowledge of and experience in human rights and commissioned by the chairperson.
(3) Where deemed necessary for the performance of its duties, the Council may request relevant public officials, experts, or other persons with specialized knowledge and experience to attend and may hear their opinions.

Article 20 (Functions of the Council)
(1) The Council shall consult on the following matters: <Amended on August 18, 2026>
1. Preparation of draft recommendations concerning the national basic plan for human rights policy;
2. Matters concerning recommendations under Articles 19, 25, 44, 45, and 48 of the Act;
3. Exchange and sharing of information on human rights;
4. Matters concerning human rights education under Article 26 of the Act;
5. Other matters necessary for the protection and promotion of human rights.
(2) The Council shall have 1 executive secretary, who shall be appointed by the chairperson from among public officials of the Commission.

Article 21 (Operation of the Council)
(1) The Council shall be convened when the Council chair deems it necessary.
(2) Members attending meetings of the Council and relevant experts and other persons who attend and speak at meetings of the Council may be paid allowances, travel expenses, and other necessary expenses within budgetary limits: Provided, That this shall not apply where a public official attends in connection with matters directly related to that official’s duties.
(3) Councils for specific fields, including human rights policy and human rights education, may be established within the Council, taking into account the expertise and distinctive characteristics of each area of work. <Inserted on August 18, 2026>
(4) Other matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Council and related matters shall be prescribed by the Commission’s rules. <Amended on August 18, 2026>

Article 21-2 (Methods of and Notification for On-site Visits to Military Units)
(1) Where the Military Human Rights Protector, a commissioner, or a member of the Commission's staff (hereinafter referred to as the "Military Human Rights Protector, etc.") visits a military unit (meaning a unit or institution established pursuant to Article 15 of the Act on the Organization of National Armed Forces; hereinafter the same shall apply) to conduct an investigation pursuant to Article 50-4 (1) of the Act, the investigation shall be conducted by the following methods:
1. Hearing statements from employees of the military unit and military personnel, etc.;
2. Requesting the head of the military unit or its employees and military personnel, etc. to submit necessary materials;
3. Taking the following measures necessary to investigate the human rights situation of military personnel, etc.:
(a) Audio recording, video recording, and photography;
(b) Examination of the health conditions of military personnel, etc.;
(c) Verification of objects, persons, places, or other circumstances.
(2) Where the Military Human Rights Protector intends to make audio or video recordings or take photographs under paragraph (1) 3 (a), the Protector shall consult in advance with the head of the military unit on their scope and subjects.
(3) Pursuant to the main clause of Article 50-4 (2) of the Act, the Military Human Rights Protector shall notify the head of a military unit to be visited in writing of the purpose, date and time, place, and other matters concerning the on-site visit no later than three days before the date of the visit.
(4) Where the Military Human Rights Protector or a commissioner intends to personally conduct an on-site visit pursuant to the proviso to Article 50-4 (2) of the Act, the Protector or commissioner shall notify the Minister of National Defense in writing of the purpose, date and time, and target military unit of the on-site visit, and other relevant matters, at least 12 hours before visiting the military unit: Provided, That where there is an urgent need to conduct an investigation on the day of notification, notification shall be given during working hours (meaning from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.) at least four hours before visiting the military unit.
(5) Where the Minister of National Defense intends to request suspension of an on-site visit pursuant to the former part of Article 50-4 (3) of the Act, the Minister shall submit a written request for suspension of the on-site visit, specifying the reasons and the period for which suspension is requested, to the Commission or the Military Human Rights Protection Committee under Article 50-3 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Commission, etc.").
(6) Notwithstanding paragraph (5), where urgent circumstances make it difficult to submit a written request for suspension of an on-site visit, the Minister of National Defense may state such circumstances and request suspension of the on-site visit by telephone, fax, email, or orally. In such cases, the Minister shall submit the written request for suspension of the on-site visit as soon as the circumstances cease to exist.
(7) Upon receiving a request for suspension of an on-site visit under paragraphs (5) and (6), the Commission, etc. shall examine the reasons and the period for which suspension is requested without delay, and notify the Minister of National Defense of the results.
(8) Article 3 (4) through (6) shall apply mutatis mutandis to restrictions on the use for other purposes and publication of audio or video recordings made during an on-site visit to a military unit under paragraph (1), and to entries in and preparation of records of on-site visits. In such cases, "commissioners, etc." shall be construed as "Military Human Rights Protector, etc.", and "detention and protective facilities" as "military units".

Article 21-3 (Procedures for Attendance at Inquiries and Investigations into Deaths of Military Personnel)
(1) Upon becoming aware of a death involving military personnel, etc., the Minister of National Defense shall immediately notify the Commission, etc. in writing of the following matters pursuant to Article 50-6 (1) of the Act:
1. An outline of the incident;
2. The unit or institution to which the deceased belonged and the deceased's rank;
3. The circumstances of discovery;
4. The date and time and place of discovery.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), in an emergency, only confirmed facts may be notified orally. In such cases, written notification shall be given immediately when the urgent circumstances cease to exist.
(3) Where the Commission, etc. intends to request the attendance of the Military Human Rights Protector and staff at an ongoing inquiry or investigation into a death pursuant to the former part of Article 50-6 (2) of the Act, it shall give advance written notice of the persons who will attend and the purpose of their attendance to the head of the military inquiry agency or military investigative agency (excluding the head of an investigative agency investigating a case involving an offense under any subparagraph of Article 2 (2) of the Military Court Act).

Article 22 (Procedures and Standards for Imposition of Administrative Fines)
(1) The procedures for imposing administrative fines under Article 63 (1) and (2) of the Act shall be governed by the Act on the Regulation of Violations of Public Order and its subordinate statutes.
(2) The standards for imposing administrative fines under Article 63 (1) and (2) of the Act shall be as specified in the Annex.

Article 23 (Processing of Personally Identifiable Information)
Where unavoidable for performing duties of investigating and providing remedies for human rights violations and discriminatory acts pursuant to subparagraphs 2 and 3 of Article 19 of the Act, the Commission may process materials containing resident registration numbers, passport numbers, and alien registration numbers under subparagraphs 1, 2, and 4 of Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 17517, February 9, 2002>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Amendments of Other Statutes)
(1) The Decree on the Appointment of Public Officials is amended as follows:
In subparagraph 4 (a) of Article 2, "Chairperson of the Central Personnel Commission" shall be replaced by "Chairperson of the Central Personnel Commission, Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission".
(2) The Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Disclosure of Military Service Records of Public Officials, etc. is amended as follows:
Subparagraph 8-2 shall be newly inserted in Article 2 as follows:
8-2. For public officials belonging to the National Human Rights Commission: The Secretariat of the National Human Rights Commission.
(3) The Regulations on Security Duties are amended as follows:
Subparagraph 3-2 shall be newly inserted in Article 7 (1) as follows:
3-2. The Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission.
